title: SovdXUpdate
description: The x-update extension to the ISO 17978-3 §7.18 software-update resource family. It adds exactly what a two-phase (activate, then decide) update needs on top of the standard resource: a registration option, a lifecycle state, the kind of reset an activation needs, four verbs, a manifest part, and a node-level observation resource. It defines no executor internals. Everything a client needs to decide is observable; nothing in this contract lets the server refuse a verdict on the client's behalf.

RegistrationOptions.title: x-update member of the registration body
RegistrationOptions.description: Nested as `x-update` in the standard POST {entity}/updates body. Absent means a standard one-phase update.

two_phase.description: Stop after activation and keep the update ACTIVATED_UNCOMMITTED until the client sends x-update-commit or x-update-rollback. Without it the server commits as part of execute.

State.title: x-update lifecycle state
State.description: Total over the life of the update resource. Each value fixes the standard `phase`/`status` pair the same status body must carry (see the table in README.md); a server never reports a pair that contradicts the state. Values are UPPER_SNAKE and never change spelling between servers.

x-descriptions.READY: Registered, or invalidated. Nothing is staged. prepare may be sent. phase=prepare status=pending.
x-descriptions.PREPARING: prepare accepted: transfer, verification and staging are running. phase=prepare status=inProgress.
x-descriptions.VALIDATED: prepare completed: the package is verified and staged, nothing is activated. execute or x-update-invalidate may be sent. phase=prepare status=completed.
x-descriptions.ACTIVATING: execute accepted: the new software is being installed or is armed but is not yet running. When reset_kind is component or node the state stays ACTIVATING until that reset has happened and the new software is observed running. phase=execute status=inProgress.
x-descriptions.ACTIVATED_UNCOMMITTED: The new software is running and a verdict is owed (two_phase only). x-update-commit or x-update-rollback may be sent. phase=execute status=inProgress.
x-descriptions.COMMITTING: x-update-commit accepted and running. phase=execute status=inProgress.
x-descriptions.COMMITTED: The new software is permanent. x-update-finish may be sent. phase=execute status=completed.
x-descriptions.ROLLING_BACK: x-update-rollback accepted and running, or the server is reverting after a failure. phase=execute status=inProgress.
x-descriptions.ROLLED_BACK: The previous software is in effect again. x-update-finish may be sent. phase=execute status=failed error.error_code=update-rolled-back.
x-descriptions.FAILED: A prepare or execute step failed and nothing is in a half state the client must resolve; details in the standard error object. x-update-finish or DELETE may be sent. status=failed in the phase that failed.
x-descriptions.FINISHED: x-update-finish completed: staged data released, the resource is kept only for reading and awaits DELETE. phase/status unchanged from the terminal state.

ResetKind.title: Reset an activation needs
ResetKind.description: Known once the package is VALIDATED. The client issues the reset; the server only reports which one. `component`: the standard PUT {component}/status/restart on this component makes the new software run. `node`: the whole node must restart, by PUT {node-entity}/status/restart on the entity that owns the node (or by any out-of-band restart such as an ignition cycle); one node restart activates every update on that node that reports `node`. `none`: the new software runs without a reset.

Status.title: x-update member of the update status body
Status.description: Nested as `x-update` in the standard GET {entity}/updates/{id}/status body (ISO 17978-3 Table 270). The standard members (phase, status, progress, step, error) keep their meaning; `state` refines them.

reset_kind.description: Present from VALIDATED on. Absent before the package is verified.

two_phase.description: Echo of the registration option, so a client that reconnects knows whether a verdict will be owed.

adopted.description: True when this resource was re-created from durable executor state by a registration with the same id (see README.md, reconnect). Absent or false otherwise.

Details.title: x-update member of the update details body
Details.description: Nested as `x-update` in the standard GET {entity}/updates/{id} body.

Verb.title: x-update verbs
Verb.description: Each is PUT {entity}/updates/{id}/<verb> with an empty body, answered 202 with a Location header to the status resource, or 409 precondition-not-fulfilled naming the current state. The precondition is a State, nothing else: a server does not refuse a verdict because of its own view of the outcome.

ManifestUploadResponse.title: Response to PUT {entity}/updates/{id}/bulk-data/manifest
ManifestUploadResponse.description: The uploaded part is the update's manifest, opaque to the server: the server stores the bytes and hands them to the executor unchanged. Verification belongs to the executor.

sha256.description: Digest of the stored bytes, so a reconnecting client can verify without a GET.

NodeUpdateState.title: Node-level observation: GET {node-entity}/data/x-update-state
NodeUpdateState.description: Everything a client needs to sequence a node restart and the verdicts after it, in one read. Facts only; the client decides.

node_boot_id.description: Opaque identifier of the node's current boot. Changes on every node restart. null when the node cannot tell.

updates.description: Every update resource on this node that is not READY and not FINISHED, in registration order.

entity.description: Path of the entity the update targets, e.g. components/host.

reboot_owed.description: Entities whose activation reported reset_kind=node and for which no verdict has been recorded yet. Persists across the restart; emptied only by commit, rollback or finish.

rebooted_since_arming.description: Whether node_boot_id differs from the one recorded when the first entry of reboot_owed was armed. null when reboot_owed is empty or the node cannot tell. false means the client has not restarted the node yet; true means it has and the verdicts may be given.

ErrorCode.title: x-update error codes
ErrorCode.description: Used in the standard error object's error_code beside the ISO codes (precondition-not-fulfilled, update-process-in-progress, ...).

x-descriptions.update-rolled-back: The update was rolled back on the client's request or by the server after a failed activation. Carried while state is ROLLED_BACK so a client that reads only the standard body sees status=failed and a reason.

Capability.title: Component capability advertisement
Capability.description: Nested as `capabilities` in the standard GET {entity-path} body of every entity that accepts updates. A client discovers update targets by listing components and keeping those with software_update=true; no vendor root attribute is needed.
